chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amer narrated to us, from his uncle 'Abdullah ibn 'Amer, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Humran ibn A'yun, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali. He said: I heard the Master of Worshippers, Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them) saying to his Shia:

You must fulfill trusts, for by He who truly sent Muhammad as a prophet, if the killer of my father al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them both) were to entrust me with the sword that he used to kill him, I would fulfill that trust to him.

key_terms.أداء: Fulfillment, discharge of duty or obligation
key_terms.الأمانة: Trust, trustworthiness - a moral and legal obligation to return what has been entrusted
key_terms.السيف: The sword - referring to the weapon used to kill Imam al-Husayn (AS) at Karbala
key_terms.سيد العابدين: Master of Worshippers - title of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Zayn al-Abidin say about fulfilling trusts even to enemies?
ai.summary: Imam Zayn al-Abidin (AS) delivered this powerful exhortation to his followers about the absolute obligation of fulfilling trusts (amanah). Speaking to his Shia community in the aftermath of the tragedy of Karbala, he swore by the One who sent Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) that even if the murderer of his own father, Imam al-Husayn (AS), entrusted him with the very sword used in the killing, he would honor that trust and return it. This hadith underscores the paramount importance of trustworthiness in Islam, demonstrating that it transcends even the deepest personal grief and enmity.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him
